The transaction costs of designing these projects are high and are based on demand. Therefore, the Peacebuilding Fund and the United Kingdom recognize the need to revisit the targets.
history.board_assessment: Given that the relevant targets are being revised, the Board considers this recommendation to be under implementation.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration intensify efforts to ensure that projects are allocated and approved in accordance with the priority windows, specifically the cross-border window.
history.administration_response: As per the recommendation of the Board, the targets for cross-border and transitions priority windows have been revised to 10 per cent for the cross-border priority window, and to within 5 per cent of the previous year’s figure for the transitions priority window. The Peacebuilding Fund has also modified the Fund guidelines to increase the duration of cross-border programming to three years. In 2023, the Fund approved 12 per cent for cross- border and regional approaches, 19 per cent for facilitating transitions, and 28 per cent for women’s and youth empowerment. This indicates that the Peacebuilding Fund exceeded the targets for the cross-border and women’s and youth empowerment priority windows. Concerning transition settings, efforts were adversely impacted by the outbreak of war in Sudan and the termination of the mandate of the United Nations Multidimensional Integrated Stabilization Mission in Mali (MINUSMA), as well as relatively lower levels of programming in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Guinea-Bissau and Sierra Leone. The Administration therefore requests closure of this recommendation.
history.board_assessment: Given that the target has been allocated and approved accordingly, the Board considers this recommendation to be implemented.
